lines.trans: Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!
Good morning again, boss! Did you forget your wallet, or did you miss me?
Salma?! Why are you standing inside a window behind the municipal clock tower?!
Because three left turns make a circle, Rami, and this is our own kitchen window!
She is right—I am making the afternoon cinnamon rolls for Jasmine Courtyard.
So the famous two-minute shortcut brings us straight back to our own starting gate.
This is impossible! We turned north, then west, then...
And then south, right back to Jasmine Street! Give the brass compass back to Tariq.
Never mind, Salma—do you smell something burning behind you?
My cinnamon rolls! Excuse me, I have to run to the oven!
We are definitely not finding the next clue if we keep walking in circles.
Let us go back to the stone fountain and try looking at Card Two again.
This time, we follow the compass—and nobody mentions shortcuts!

Goodbye!

meanings.note: Used to express certainty or agreement.

examples.trans: I will certainly come to the party.

examples.text: أكيد ما رح أنسى أجبلك الكتاب بكرة الصبح.
examples.trans: For sure I won't forget to bring you the book tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: أنا وإياك رح نخلص المشروع قبل يوم الخميس.
examples.trans: You and I will finish the project before Thursday.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or confirmation in Jordanian conversation.

examples.text: أها! هلق فهمت ليش الباب ما كان يفتح.
examples.trans: Aha! Now I understand why the door would not open.

examples.text: أها، إنت اللي خبيت المفتاح تحت الصحن!
examples.trans: Aha, you are the one who hid the key under the plate!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Used constantly in the polite phrase عن إذنك ('excuse me / with your permission').

examples.trans: Excuse me, may I pass?
He asked permission before heading out.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb; frequently used in imperatives for following directions or clues.

examples.text: اتبعوا الخريطة خطوة بخطوة عشان ما تضيعوا.
examples.trans: Follow the map step by step so you do not get lost.

examples.text: دايما بنتبع البوصلة لما نمشي بالزقاق.
examples.trans: We always follow the compass when we walk through the alley.

meanings.note: Used in everyday speech for a shorter route as well as a shortened word.

examples.text: رامي دايما بلاقي اختصار سريع من ورا الساحة.
examples.trans: Rami always finds a quick shortcut behind the courtyard.

examples.text: بلاش نجرب أي اختصار واحنا مستعجلين.
examples.trans: Let us not try any shortcut while we are in a hurry.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتاق, بيشتاق).

examples.trans: I missed you so much over these three years.
We missed our Friday gatherings.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Form VII passive/inchoative of حرق.

examples.text: انتبهي عالفرن عشان الكيكة ما تنحرق!
examples.trans: Watch the oven so the cake does not burn!

examples.text: شامة ريحة إشي عم ينحرق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: I smell something burning in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببدا, بيبدا).

examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.
The day began lively and bright.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical tower, a skyscraper, or an astrological sign.

examples.trans: This is the highest tower in the city.

examples.text: برج الساعة القديم مبين من فوق السطوح.
examples.trans: The old clock tower is visible from the rooftop.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Used for navigation or metaphorically for direction.

examples.text: ضاع بالصحراء لأنه ما كان معه بوصلة.
examples.trans: He got lost in the desert because he didn't have a compass.

examples.text: اتبعنا إبرة البوصلة لحد ما وصلنا الشرق.
examples.trans: We followed the compass needle until we reached the east.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from تاريخ (history), agreeing with الساحة.

examples.text: وسط البلد فيه مباني تاريخية عمرها أكتر من مية سنة.
examples.trans: Downtown has historic buildings that are over a hundred years old.

examples.text: المدرج الروماني معلم تاريخي مهم بعمان.
examples.trans: The Roman Theater is an important historic landmark in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: The number 3 when followed by a counted noun.

examples.trans: I have three cars in the garage.

examples.text: مشينا تلات دقايق وبعدين وصلنا عالبوابة.
examples.trans: We walked three minutes and then reached the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guests arrived from the south in the morning.
The weather is warm in the south today.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Go inside the house, the weather is cold.
The metal tin is hidden inside the cupboard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحاول, بيحاول).

examples.trans: I tried to smile as hard as I could!
We tried to find a quick solution.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: We found a strange stone in the garden.

examples.text: لقينا حجر منحوت عليه نجمة صغيرة.
examples.trans: We found a stone with a small star carved on it.

meanings.note: Used in معك حق ('you are right / you have a point').

examples.trans: You are right, the weather is cold today.
Everyone has a right to rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دوائر.

examples.trans: A paper arrived from the property department.
The department office is downtown.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Walk straight and then turn right.

examples.text: امشي دغري لعند القوس وبعدين لف يسار.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the arch and then turn left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Can mean evidence, proof, or a guide (both a person and a guidebook).

examples.trans: Do you have evidence for what you're saying?

examples.text: هادا الرقم الصغير هو أول دليل للوصول للكنز.
examples.trans: This small number is the first clue for reaching the treasure.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: She came running back across the overpass in ten minutes.
Running in the morning energises the body.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: روايح.

examples.trans: The aroma of coffee in the morning is wonderful!
The scent of cinnamon reaches the second floor.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Used in جاب سيرة ('to bring up / mention a topic').

examples.text: لا حدا يجيب سيرة الشغل عالعشا!
examples.trans: Nobody bring up work at dinner!
Everyone speaks kindly of you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Feminine imperative of شمّ (to smell), addressing Salma.

examples.text: شمّي ريحة القرفة والهيل طالعة من الفرن!
examples.trans: Smell the scent of cinnamon and cardamom coming out of the oven!

examples.text: بحب أشمّ هوا نضيف بالحديقة الصبح.
examples.trans: I love breathing in fresh air in the garden in the morning.

meanings.note: Standard word for morning in both Classical and colloquial Arabic.

examples.trans: The weather is nice this morning.

examples.text: نسمات الصباح بالحديقة بتجيب ريحة الياسمين.
examples.trans: The morning breezes in the garden carry the scent of jasmine.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: He stayed at home and didn't go out.

examples.text: ضل الدفتر مفتوح عالطاولة طول الليل.
examples.trans: The notebook remained open on the table all night.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Cardinal direction noun paired with شرق (east); used with directional prepositions like للغرب.

examples.text: البوابة التانية بتطلع على جهة الغرب.
examples.trans: The second gate faces toward the west.

examples.text: امشوا عشر خطوات للغرب بتلاقوا العلامة.
examples.trans: Walk ten steps to the west and you will find the mark.

meanings.note: With demonstrative هـ + الـ, هالفترة means 'during this period / right now'.

examples.trans: I'm very busy these days.
A hard period passed over us.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: The warm scent of cinnamon filled the kitchen.
We ate a cinnamon roll with tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.trans: I want tea, and also coffee.

examples.text: ذقنا التانية وكمان التالتة عشان نقارن القوام.
examples.trans: We tasted the second one and also the third to compare the texture.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

لاقى.gloss: to find; to encounter; to meet

meanings.en: to find; to encounter; to meet
meanings.note: Form III defective verb widely used in Jordanian Arabic as the everyday verb meaning to find (alongside لقي).

examples.text: أخيرا لاقينا المفتاح الضاع تحت السجادة.
examples.trans: We finally found the lost key under the rug.

examples.text: إذا دورت منيح بالدرج بتلاقي الكرت.
examples.trans: If you look carefully in the drawer you will find the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Plural of لفافة ('roll/scroll'), used in bakeries for cinnamon rolls.

examples.text: عملت سلمى لفائف قرفة سخنة مع سكر ناعم عالوجه.
examples.trans: Salma made warm cinnamon rolls with powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: لقينا لفافة ورق قديمة مربوطة بخيط جوا الصندوق.
examples.trans: We found an old paper scroll tied with string inside the box.

meanings.note: Used in Jordan to mean a wrap or a sandwich (e.g. falafel or shawarma), or a turn in the road.

examples.trans: I want a falafel sandwich with fries.

examples.text: أخذنا لفة سريعة بالسوق واشترينا زعتر وفستق.
examples.trans: We took a quick stroll around the market and bought thyme and pistachios.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why were you late to work today?

examples.text: ليش الحبر على طرف الورقة مبين أغمق من النص؟
examples.trans: Why does the ink at the edge of the sheet look darker than the middle?

meanings.note: A very common Jordanian way to say 'no one' or 'nobody'.

examples.text: محدش كان في البيت لما رنيت.
examples.trans: Nobody was at home when I called.

examples.text: محدش شاف مين حط البطاقة الخامسة جوا الكتاب.
examples.trans: Nobody saw who placed the fifth card inside the book.

meanings.note: Noun of place/instrument from حفظ (to keep/guard); covers pocket wallets, purses, and school satchels.

examples.text: كان في ورقة مطوية جوا محفظة الجلد.
examples.trans: There was a folded paper inside the leather wallet.
I forgot my wallet on the table in the lobby.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: مديرة). Plural: مدراء.

examples.trans: She became the permanent front-desk manager at the guesthouse.
The manager welcomed the new guests.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: I went to Petra one time.

examples.text: جربنا الوصفة مرة تانية بس بخففنا السكر شوي.
examples.trans: We tried the recipe one more time, though we reduced the sugar slightly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستحيلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
It is impossible for us to forget this week.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: I am not upset with you.

examples.text: هادا المفتاح مش للباب الرئيسي، هادا للخزانة.
examples.trans: This key is not for the main door; this one is for the cupboard.

meanings.note: البنت المشهورة describes Layan's high-profile popularity across school.

examples.trans: Layan is well-known across the whole school.
This is a famous restaurant in Amman.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مهمة, plural: مهمين).

examples.text: يوم الجمعة يوم مهم كتير إلي.
examples.trans: Friday is a very important day for me.
I have an important note at the bottom of the page.

meanings.note: Used for decorative water fountains in parks or squares.

examples.trans: There is a beautiful fountain in the park.

examples.text: نافورة المي اللي بنص الساحة صوتها هادي ومريح.
examples.trans: The water fountain in the middle of the courtyard has a calm, soothing sound.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: This jug is made of copper.

examples.text: الإبريق والمصفاية معمولين من نحاس مطروق قديم.
examples.trans: The teapot and strainer are made of old hammered copper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: The car is behind the house.

examples.text: الحديقة موجودة ورا المبنى بعيدة عن عجقة الشارع.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the building, away from the street traffic.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Not even one of them came.

examples.text: سألت الكل بس ولا حدا بيعرف وين حطوا المفتاح.
examples.trans: I asked everyone, yet not a single person knows where they put the key.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Direction noun synonymous with شمال (left) in urban speech; frequently used as عاليسار (on the left).

examples.text: المكتبة موجودة على جهة اليسار بعد القوس.
examples.trans: The library is on the left side right after the arch.

examples.text: لفوا يسار عند النافورة بتلاقوا الممر.
examples.trans: Turn left at the fountain and you will find the passage.
